study.question: At unchanged fixed-state predictions, capacity and history compression, does removing the product RMS scale derivative improve click validation AUC, and does its effect interact with auxiliary adapter-context transfer?
study.hypothesis: Observed source limitation: the incumbent computes x=q*s for a task context query q and a masked blockwise nonlinear history summary s, then y=x/sqrt(mean(x^2)+1e-4). The scale derivative couples all 16 coordinates. This is a source-derived property, not measured gradient conflict, saturation or instability. Local performance evidence: g0-r0039-context_product beats its sum alternative (0.668457308 vs 0.664563151), and g0-r0052-block_nonlinear_transfer beats blocked transfer (0.668526868 vs 0.667868134). Later aligned/permuted details both lose to the broadcast bridge (0.668471309/0.668444544 vs 0.668526868), so no useful block-detail association is established. The new hypothesis is that suppressing only the per-example normalization-scale derivative preserves useful signed coordinate updates into compressed-history/context projections and may improve auxiliary-context transfer under the frozen one-pass recipe. Predict detached_transfer exceeds live_transfer and has a more favorable effect with transfer than without. This is a provisional learning-rule hypothesis, with no guarantee of improvement.

nearest_work.difference: Read archived primary text lines56..115 on target-dependent local activation and fixed-vector bottlenecks. Retain this inherited target scorer, not a new DIN contribution; intervene only in a downstream task-specific product normalization VJP.

Pinned benchmark source lines194..313 uses multi-view hub aggregation, affine gated broadcasting and LayerNorm after residuals. No hub, attention or LayerNorm component adopted. Here the existing rank16 product forward map is fixed and its scalar RMS derivative is the intervention. Original INFNet paper detail is unavailable via paper:infnet; no original-paper equivalence or priority claim.

Pinned source lines174..213 instantiates LayerNorm around token/FFN blocks; no token mixer adopted. This proposal changes a gradient edge of an existing product without new tokens or forward expressivity.
Pinned source lines175..214 shows ID/attribute projections with LayerNorm and mixer norms; no embedding expansion adopted. All embedding widths and counts are inherited.

Exact candidate.py SHA2568510b32102c1bdce1338328127aef1e4241c4cf592c7f123f551bae0e733ae4a reproduced. Preserve the whole model and change only the product scale derivative; cross with its existing auxiliary adapter-context gate.

Earlier projection of aggregate auxiliary context cotangents was worse than its full bridge (0.666906896 vs0.667057510). That acts in source embedding space across adapters; this intervention acts inside each task rank16 product on both context/history projections. Negative result limits general claims about removing radial gradients.

The tanh-forward/softsign-derivative cell lost to tanh/tanh (0.668314736 vs0.668526868). Keep tanh derivatives unchanged; test only normalization denominator differentiation. Surrogate-gradient ideas themselves are established; originality unverified. Authorized RMSNorm source search returned no matches, not evidence of novelty.

inherited_components: All frozen sample inputs, masks, action visibility, four labels, BCE, seed, epochs, precision, optimizers, loading and scorers.
All incumbent embeddings, folded support-Dice scorer, independent auxiliary moments, ten-block compression, signed primary/feedback bases, counts and five moments.
All task residual adapters, context queries, tied blockwise tanh history projections, normalized signed products, zero-initialized interaction outputs and four Dice towers.

Same source ownership: auxiliary scorer/item/action/target and tower-context gradients blocked; existing adapter-context gate supplies the second factor. Same module construction/order, state shapes, initialization and RNG.
study.proposed_difference: Only a product_scale_gradient architecture option live/detached is added. In FP32 let a=rsqrt(mean(x*x)+eps), eps=1e-4 and k=1(live) or0(detached). Form a_used=a.detach()+k*(a-a.detach()), then y=x*a_used. All cells execute identical operators. At finite common x the forward equals x*a exactly; no new parameters/buffers/RNG. For upstream g and d=16, live VJP is a*g - (a^3/d)*x*dot(g,x), detached VJP is a*g. The latter is an intentionally declared surrogate derivative, not the exact gradient of the normalized BCE forward objective. Cross k with the existing auxiliary adapter-context enabled/blocked factor; all task products receive the selected rule, while blocked source edges stay blocked. The factor concerns RMS of the product, not the folded Dice population or history coefficient normalization.
predictions: At common nonzero interaction-output weights and identical state, all four cells have identical forward outputs and all primary/auxiliary Dice buffer updates. Live bridges match their inherited references in predictions, VJPs and one optimizer step within declared dtype tolerance; the auxiliary gate changes only its owned source VJP.

Detached scale VJP adds (a^3/d)*x*dot(g,x) relative to live. Tangent g perpendicular to x has the same VJP; radial live VJP is eps*a^3*g whereas detached is a*g. At x=0 both equal100*g. No denominator-induced cross-coordinate term survives detached mode.

Predict AUC(detached_transfer)>AUC(live_transfer). Transfer-specific support additionally requires I=[AUC(detached_transfer)-AUC(live_transfer)]-[AUC(detached_blocked)-AUC(live_blocked)]>0, with uncertainty unresolved at the frozen single seed.

All cells have expected32192421 total/31793216 embedding/399205 dense parameters. Measured training, allocated GPU, inference and wall costs determine whether any predictive advantage is worthwhile; parameter equality alone does not establish equal compute.
falsifiers: No click AUC gain for detached_transfer over the live bridge falsifies useful improvement for this implementation/recipe. A lower auxiliary mean or higher logloss is retained as a tradeoff even if click improves.

I<=0 fails the predicted beneficial interaction with auxiliary-context transfer. Similar detached gains in both gate settings support a generic optimization effect rather than transfer-specific explanation; I>0 alone does not establish the proposed gradient mechanism.

Any common-state forward, masks, source ownership, buffer, parameter or RNG mismatch beyond declared tolerances invalidates the intended contrast until corrected through authorized execution. Missing native validation is not a model failure.

A gain explained by gradient magnitude, dense clipping or Adagrad dynamics cannot establish beneficial cross-coordinate direction; reserve a norm-matched VJP control before making that stronger claim. Repeated seeded studies are required for repeated support.
alternative_explanations: Detached denominator generally increases product cotangent norm; dense clipping, sparse repeated-ID accumulation and AdamW/Adagrad may explain gains. This factorial does not norm-match gradients or optimizer updates.
One seed, one data pass, many prior validation selections and BF16 rounding can yield selection noise; deterministic replay is not independent replication.
The auxiliary gate covers both residual and product adapter context paths. Interaction is between whole declared switches, not exclusive proof about the product source edge.

Frozen official_offline histories and auxiliary category/brand24h labels limit point-in-time and conversion interpretation. Sparse auxiliary outcomes and auxiliary quality regressions may accompany click selection.

Earlier softsign surrogate, context radial/tangent, moment closure, pair and detail-alignment branches were unsuccessful predictive trajectories. Their failure motivates a narrow falsifiable test, not a general claim that normalization gradients are harmful.
